title: Domain modules import no runtime machinery

facts.note: File path carries a `domain/` layer segment; files with no layer segment are out of scope. Applies to any in-scope domain module, whether the offending import is new or already present.
Excluding test files and vendored/build directories, which are never scanned.
Observer for import specifiers / `Bun.` global references present in a domain module (existing or newly added); currently established by bun_clean_architecture_detector findings.
Detector finding surfaced to the agent.

fires: A non-test module under `domain/` imports `bun:sqlite`, `node:fs` or any other `bun:*`/`node:*` specifier (newly added or already present).
A domain module references the `Bun.` global (e.g. `Bun.env`, `Bun.file`).
doesNotFire: Files in vendored or build output directories.
A file whose path carries no layer segment.
An infrastructure or presentation module importing `bun:*`, `node:*` or an HTTP framework.

given: A non-test, non-vendored/build module in the `domain/` layer
when: it imports a specifier or references a global (new or existing)
then: It MUST NOT import runtime machinery (`bun:*`, `node:*`, `htmx`, `express`, `fastify`, `koa`) nor reach the `Bun.` global.
prefer: Keep domain code as data-in / data-out logic.
Move Bun, Node, htmx, server, or framework machinery to an outer layer and pass the needed value inward.

During GREEN: adapt at the nearest existing integration or presentation boundary, passing the smallest value or domain-facing collaborator the behavior needs; add a new boundary only when no existing one can express the current behavior correctly.
avoid: Wrapping a framework API in a domain-named helper and keeping the coupling.
Importing runtime machinery just to satisfy the acceptance quickly.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules, not in violation.
why: The domain expresses rules, not machinery; for a full-stack Bun app the machinery is the server and transport primitives. The domain must be runnable with no server started — `Bun.` in a domain module means it is not.
evidence: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no framework/runtime import specifier and no `Bun.` global use in any domain module.
The domain remains executable without runtime machinery (runnable with no server started).
verifier_detail: Flag framework/runtime import specifiers in a domain module, and any use of the `Bun.` global.

runtime_machinery = `bun:*`, `node:*`, an HTTP framework (`htmx`, `express`, `fastify`, `koa`), or the `Bun.` global — this stack's equivalent of the UI frameworks the Vite sibling forbids (react/preact/@tanstack/gsap); the obligation is identical and only the list of machinery changes with the stack.
server_free_domain = the practical test: the domain must be runnable with no server started.
Do not scan test files or vendored/build directories.

Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked (layer-direction checks only apply to project-internal specifiers; the named framework specifiers above are still matched by this rule's list).
A file carrying no layer segment is out of scope, not a violation.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Vite sibling forbids react/preact/@tanstack/gsap because those are ITS frameworks.

sharedNodes.text: During GREEN: add a new boundary only when no existing one can express the current behavior correctly. Do not broaden: do not redesign adjacent layers. Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire examples (e.g. `bun:test` in a test file, `Bun.env`, infrastructure modules importing machinery).
additions.justification: Concrete activation boundaries derived directly from the statement and exceptions; no new obligation.

additions.text: Clarification that the bare-npm-specifier exception concerns layer-direction checks, not the named framework list.
additions.justification: Without it, S033 would contradict the htmx/express/fastify/koa bans, which are bare npm specifiers.

trace.note: GREEN qualifier kept as prefix of prefer[2] and in the shared node.
Rule-specific: nearest existing integration or presentation boundary stays in this rule.
Rule-specific: smallest value or domain-facing collaborator passed into the domain stays in this rule.
Kept as the bare source label 'strict' without added semantics.
